clue.text: Come down to earth about p-payment for a sweet

indicators.note: about means going round, so the toppling word is wrapped round the next pieces

parts.note: to topple is to fall over, coming down to the ground
the stammered p- tells us to stammer a word for payment: F-FEE

explanation.surface: Someone is brought back to reality by a stammered demand for payment for a sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated 'p-' mimics a stammer, so the payment word is stammered too; 'about' wraps the fall-over word round that and the A. 'for' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A toffee apple is a confection: an apple coated in hard toffee on a stick, a fairground treat.

clue.text: See 7
Picture of the king of the fuzz?

parts.note: flic is French slang for a police officer, as fuzz is English slang for the police
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A question about a portrait of the top police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: The king letter goes after the police word, since the K belongs to (is 'of') the fuzz.
explanation.definitionFit: A flick is informal for a film or movie, a moving picture.

clue.text: Raise Balkan money to cite a school in Battersea

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising means reading the pieces from the bottom up, so they are reversed

parts.note: the leu is the currency of Romania
to cite something is to name it

explanation.surface: An instruction to lift a Balkan currency in order to quote a London school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise' reverses both pieces together: LEU and NAME read upwards give EMAN then UEL. Battersea is a district of south London.
explanation.definitionFit: Emanuel School is a long-established independent school in Battersea, south London.

clue.text: Plant for bestial characters

indicators.note: the letters (characters) of the word bestial are taken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A plant suited to brutish personalities.
explanation.definitionFit: Astilbe is a garden perennial with feathery plumes of flowers.

clue.text: Allow publication of purchasing record

parts.note: to pass something is to allow or approve it
a book is a publication

explanation.surface: Permission is given to publish an account of what was bought.
explanation.definitionFit: A passbook is a small book recording a customer's deposits and withdrawals, a record of transactions.

clue.text: Non-stop percussion instrument fraught with problems

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase describing the noun phrase, which is a relationship full of trouble

parts.note: non-stop means everlasting, eternal
a triangle is a metal percussion instrument

explanation.surface: A drummer's instrument that never stops causing trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes the answer rather than naming it: the relationship is one that is always fraught.
explanation.definitionFit: An eternal triangle is a love affair involving three people, a situation notoriously full of jealousy and conflict.

clue.text: Turning? Caesar's not that sort (thinner man)

definitions.text: Turning? Caesar's not that sort (thinner man)

indicators.note: turning suggests the following letters spin round into a new order

parts.note: the possessive s counts as a letter here

explanation.surface: Caesar declares he is not one to turn, unlike the lean man he distrusts.
explanation.walkthrough: All 28 letters of CAESARS NOT THAT SORT THINNER MAN are rearranged. In Shakespeare's Julius Caesar, Caesar says he is unmoving like the pole star, and distrusts lean Cassius.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar's boast that he never turns from his purpose, quoted from Shakespeare, matches the clue's 'not that sort' for turning.

clue.text: Economist is allowed unction (clue: home is unfinished)

parts.note: may expresses permission: you may means you are allowed
nard (spikenard) is an aromatic ointment, an unction
a key is a clue to a puzzle

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter of the word for home is dropped

parts.note: a nest is a home

explanation.surface: An economist is permitted ointment, with a parenthetical cryptic aside about a home.
explanation.definitionFit: John Maynard Keynes was the influential British economist behind Keynesian economics.

clue.text: Land of soul with money, in others' words

parts.note: âme is French for soul
rica is Spanish for rich, having money

explanation.surface: A country of the spirit and wealth, described in foreign languages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in others' words' tells you the pieces are foreign: French AME and Spanish RICA.
explanation.definitionFit: America is a land, a country or continent.

clue.text: Period novel heroine on the tile?

parts.note: Tess is the heroine of Hardy's novel Tess of the d'Urbervilles
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A heroine from a period novel sits on the roof tiles.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' places the heroine before the period.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is a small square tile used in mosaic work.

clue.text: Having no room for wine if I leave during killing

indicators.note: during puts the wine and remaining letter inside the killing word

parts.note: a cull is a selective killing of animals
hock is a German white wine

indicators.note: leave tells us the letter named just before departs from the word if

explanation.surface: No room for wine if one must leave during a massacre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if I leave' is a little deletion inside the clue: the word 'if' loses its I, leaving one letter to follow the wine, and 'during' puts both inside the killing.
explanation.definitionFit: Chock-full means crammed to capacity, so there is no space left.

clue.text: African country to second 9's backing

parts.note: B is second in the alphabet

indicators.note: backing means the word for 9 is written in reverse

parts.note: the number nine spelt out

explanation.surface: Supporting a motion about an African country in a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: '9' looks like a reference to 9-across but is simply the number, spelt and reversed to ENIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Benin is a country in West Africa.

clue.text: A B C D F or G?

definitions.text: A B C D F or G?

parts.words: A B C D F or G
parts.note: each letter listed names a musical pitch, and the list skips E

explanation.surface: A list of letters, oddly missing one.
explanation.walkthrough: Every letter given is a musical one, and the list is everything from A to G except E: read as NOT E.
explanation.definitionFit: Each letter A to G names a musical pitch, so any one of them is a musical sound.

clue.text: Group retaining changed locale for manual working

indicators.note: retaining means holding, so the group's name surrounds the other letters

parts.note: Blur is a British rock group

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of locale are rearranged

explanation.surface: A band holds on to a new venue for physical work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group' is not a generic word for a collection: it is the Britpop band, cut open by 'retaining' to hold ECOLLA, the letters of 'locale' that 'changed' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue-collar describes manual or industrial labour, as opposed to office work.

clue.text: Sound wrong to get up in the morning? This puts us first

parts.note: a hum is a sound

indicators.note: in places the reversed piece inside the morning letters

parts.note: a.m. stands for ante meridiem, the morning

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means reading the word upwards, reversed

parts.note: a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: A complaint about the noise of getting out of bed early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound wrong' reads as one idea but splits: the noise, then the misdeed, which 'to get up' turns to NIS in this down clue before 'in' puts it inside the morning letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Humanism is a philosophy putting human interests, people like us, at the centre rather than gods.

clue.text: Causing much embarrassment to the English, a Scottish game

parts.note: taken as written
curling, sliding stones on ice, is a game of Scottish origin

explanation.surface: A Scottish pastime that makes the English cringe.
explanation.definitionFit: Toe-curling describes something so embarrassing that it makes you cringe.

clue.text: Where to read Hannibal's name

parts.note: Hannibal Lecter is the cannibal of The Silence of the Lambs

explanation.surface: A question about where to read the Carthaginian general's name.
explanation.walkthrough: Hannibal suggests the general who crossed the Alps, but it is Lecter.
explanation.definitionFit: A lectern is a stand for books from which one reads aloud, as in church.

clue.text: Starting point for climb

parts.note: N (north) is a compass point
an ascent is a climb

explanation.surface: Where a mountain climb begins.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascent means just coming into being, beginning to develop.

clue.text: Journey of 3 kilometres to Rome?

parts.note: tre is Italian for three, signalled by 'to Rome'
K is the abbreviation for kilometres

explanation.surface: A short walk to the Italian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to Rome?' tells you to say the number in Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: A trek is a long, arduous journey, especially on foot.

clue.text: Martial artist is some man in Japan

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fighter is a certain Japanese man.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninja was a Japanese warrior trained in stealth and the martial arts.

clue.text: Being a fool in company and cautious, I don't fly

indicators.note: in puts the fool word inside the company letters

parts.note: an ass is a fool
wary means cautious

explanation.surface: Someone foolish but careful in company refuses to board a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: The cassowary is a large flightless bird of New Guinea and Australia, speaking in the first person.

clue.text: Girl first after love letter

indicators.note: after places the girl and first pieces behind the love letter

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, O
Meg is a girl's name
A is first in the alphabet, or first-class

explanation.surface: A girl's first love letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: A step like a colossus?

parts.note: a stride is a long step

explanation.surface: Taking a step the way a giant statue does.
explanation.walkthrough: The Colossus of Rhodes was said to stand with legs apart over the harbour mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Astride means with legs on either side, the posture legend gives the Colossus of Rhodes.

clue.text: Nurse protected by sword is the centrepiece

indicators.note: protected by means surrounded by, so the nurse goes inside the sword

parts.note: an épée is a fencing sword
RGN is Registered General Nurse

explanation.surface: A nurse guarded by a swordsman is the star attraction.
explanation.definitionFit: An epergne is an ornamental stand used as a table centrepiece, holding fruit or flowers.

clue.text: Protest involving mean rotters

indicators.note: involving suggests the letters of mean rotters are twisted together into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that drags in some nasty people.
explanation.definitionFit: To remonstrate is to protest forcefully or argue in opposition.
